history.dynasty: Pallavas (Mahendravarman I, 7th century) for the initial rock-cutting; later completed by the Nayaks of Madurai under the Vijayanagara Empire
history.period: 7th century CE (Pallava work); temples completed in the Nayak period
history.summary: The Ucchi Pillayar (Uchipillaiyar) Temple is the summit shrine of the Rockfort temple complex atop an 83-m rock in Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) - a granite outcrop estimated at ~3.8 billion years old, among the oldest rocks in the world. The smooth rock was first cut by the Pallavas (two rock-cut cave temples: the upper Lalitankura Pallavesvaram Griham of Mahendravarman I and the lower Pandyan-era cave) and the temples were completed by the Nayaks of Madurai under the Vijayanagara Empire. Legend: this is where Ganesha ran from Vibhishana after establishing the Ranganatha idol at Srirangam - the same Vibhishana-Ranganatha legend as 946 (Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangam). The complex holds three main shrines: Manikka Vinayakar at the foot, the large Thayumanaswamy (Shiva) temple mid-way (6th century, per some sources, housing Shiva and Mattuvar Kuzhalammai), and Ucchi Pillayar at the summit reached by ~437-473 rock-cut steps. It offers panoramic views of Trichy, Srirangam and the Kaveri and Kollidam rivers. The hill was fortified and saw battles between the Madurai Nayaks and the Bijapur/Carnatic forces and the British in the Carnatic Wars; the ancient cave temples are maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Ucchi Pillayar Temple
town_description: Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) is a major city in central Tamil Nadu on the Kaveri river. The Rockfort is its iconic central landmark; the temple complex is in the old-city area, about 2-3 km from Tiruchirappalli Junction. The summit view takes in the whole city, Srirangam and both rivers.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaivism - Thayumanavar; Ganesha shrines; rock-cut Pallava/Nayak)

travel.road: In the city centre of Trichy; reachable by city bus, auto and taxi.
